*tex-snippets*  Local LaTeX snippets

These LuaSnip snippets load for TeX buffers. VimTeX supplies syntax/context
information. Math snippets expand only in math, excluding comments, verbatim,
and text inside \text{...}. Typing a literal command such as \sum is preserved.

Navigation ~
    CTRL-K      Expand a manual snippet, or jump to the next placeholder.
    CTRL-J      Jump to the previous placeholder.

Most triggers below expand automatically as soon as you type them. Letter-only
triggers require a word boundary. The ; symbols, __ and ^^ also work directly
after a variable. You supply spaces and punctuation after leaving inline math.

Math entry and delimiters ~
    mk          $...$                       In prose
    dm          \[ ... \]                   At the start of a prose line
    lr          \left(...\right)            In math

Math structures (automatic, in math) ~
    ff          \frac{numerator}{denominator}
    sr          \sqrt{...}
    __          _{...}                      For example, x__
    ^^          ^{...}                      For example, x^^
    sum         \sum_{i=1}^{n} ...           Limits are editable
    int         \int_{a}^{b} ...\,\mathrm{d}x
    lim         \lim_{n \to \infty} ...
    tt          \text{...}
    mat         Two-by-two pmatrix
    cases       Two-row cases environment

Greek alphabet (automatic, in math) ~
    ;al / ;Al  alpha / Alpha       ;be / ;Be  beta / Beta
    ;ga / ;Ga  gamma / Gamma       ;de / ;De  delta / Delta
    ;ep / ;Ep  epsilon / Epsilon   ;ze / ;Ze  zeta / Zeta
    ;et / ;Et  eta / Eta           ;th / ;Th  theta / Theta
    ;io / ;Io  iota / Iota         ;ka / ;Ka  kappa / Kappa
    ;la / ;La  lambda / Lambda     ;mu / ;Mu  mu / Mu
    ;nu / ;Nu  nu / Nu             ;xi / ;Xi  xi / Xi
    ;oc / ;Oc  omicron / Omicron   ;pi / ;Pi  pi / Pi
    ;rh / ;Rh  rho / Rho           ;si / ;Si  sigma / Sigma
    ;ta / ;Ta  tau / Tau           ;up / ;Up  upsilon / Upsilon
    ;ph / ;Ph  phi / Phi           ;ch / ;Ch  chi / Chi
    ;ps / ;Ps  psi / Psi           ;om / ;Om  omega / Omega

Every uppercase trigger also has an unprefixed manual alias: Th CTRL-K inserts
\Theta, Ga CTRL-K inserts \Gamma, etc. These aliases appear in completion.
The ;ep trigger keeps its existing \varepsilon shape. Lowercase omicron is o.
Capitals with Latin-shaped glyphs use \mathrm{A}, \mathrm{B}, etc.; this avoids
undefined commands such as \Alpha in standard LaTeX.

Other symbols (automatic, in math) ~
    ;in in        ;le leq       ;ge geq       ;ne neq
    ;to to        ;iff iff      ;oo infty

Symbol expansions include a trailing space to terminate the TeX command.

Number sets and fonts (in math) ~
    RR NN ZZ QQ CC      Automatic: \mathbb{R}, etc.
    bb CTRL-K          Manual: \mathbb{...}
    cal CTRL-K         Manual: \mathcal{...}

Environments (at the beginning of a prose line, indentation allowed) ~
    ali                 Automatic: a two-row align* environment
    beg CTRL-K          Manual: \begin{...} / \end{...}, with mirrored names

Data-science course notation                                      *tex-data-science*

These additions target probability, sketching/streaming, geometry, linear
algebra, optimization, privacy, attention, and distributed algorithms.
They are available in all TeX math buffers. Defaults are editable placeholders;
repeated variables in longer formulas update together. CTRL-K advances and
CTRL-J moves backward. See LuaSnip/tex/data_science.lua to customize notation.

Automatic probability notation ~
    prb         \Pr[A]                         Probability of an event
    prx         \Pr_{h\sim\mathcal{H}}[A]       Randomness in the subscript
    cpr         \Pr[A | B]                     Conditional probability
    exv         \mathbb{E}[X]                  Expectation
    cex         \mathbb{E}[X | Y]              Conditional expectation
    var         \operatorname{Var}[X]          Variance
    cov         \operatorname{Cov}(X,Y)        Covariance
    ind         \mathbf{1}_{\{A\}}             Indicator (no extra font package)

Automatic geometry, sets, and estimates ~
    nrm         p-norm; default index 2 is editable
    nr2         Squared Euclidean norm
    nrF         Frobenius norm
    abs         Absolute value or cardinality
    inn         Inner product of two editable expressions
    set         Braced set
    sbt         Set builder: {element | condition}
    ceil / flr  Ceiling / floor
    idx         [n], with editable n
    vct         \boldsymbol{x}; also works for Greek letters
    hat / til   \widehat{x} / \widetilde{x}
    prod        Product with editable lower limit, upper limit, and body

Additional automatic symbols ~
    ;fa forall     ;ex exists     ;ni notin      ;sb subseteq
    ;cu cup        ;ca cap        ;es emptyset   ;cd cdot
    ;tm times      ;ot otimes     ;ap approx     ;sm sim
    ;sc succeq     ;pc preceq     ;as gets       ;pt propto
    ;nb nabla      ;pd partial    ;ell ell      ;df := (relation spacing)
    ;iid          iid sampling relation (iid above \sim)

The following groups are MANUAL: type the trigger, then CTRL-K, or accept the
completion. Short autosnippets do not intercept these longer trigger names.

Complexity and combinatorics (manual) ~
    bigO / bigOmega / bigTheta      O(...), \Omega(...), \Theta(...)
    littleo / littleomega           o(...), \omega(...)
    softO                           \widetilde{O}(...) (hidden log factors)
    logb                            Logarithm with editable base and argument
    binom                           Binomial coefficient, n choose k

Distributions (manual) ~
    normal      Normal: mean and variance (or vector mean and covariance)
    bern        Bernoulli: success probability
    binomial    Binomial: number of trials and success probability
    poisson     Poisson: rate
    laplace     Laplace: location and scale, initially 0 and b
    uniform     Uniform: support set or interval

Linear algebra and optimization (manual) ~
    trans / pinv       Transpose / pseudoinverse
    rank / trace       Matrix rank / trace
    diag / span        Diagonal matrix / linear span
    supp / nnz         Support / number of nonzero entries
    argmin / argmax    Optimizing variable/domain and objective
    grad / pdv         Gradient / partial derivative
    proj               Projection onto an editable set
    opt                Aligned objective and constraints for LP/SDP or other
                       optimization problems; replace the example constraint
    lsq                Least-squares argmin ||Ax-b||_2^2
    svd                A = U Sigma V^T; edit factors for a rank-k approximation
    gdstep             x_{t+1} = x_t - eta_t grad f(x_t)
    sgdstep            x_{t+1} = x_t - eta_t g_t
    regret             External regret against the best fixed action in X

Course expressions (manual) ~
    fmom        Frequency moment: sum |f_i|^p over nonzero coordinates
    lsh         Probability over h that h(x) = h(y)
    jl          Two-sided squared-distance preservation inequality
    relerr      (1-epsilon) C <= C_hat <= (1+epsilon) C
    streamwin   Ordered window (x_{t-w+1}, ..., x_t)
    dpineq      Pr[M(D) in S] <= exp(epsilon) Pr[M(D') in S] + delta
    sens        Global p-norm sensitivity; p defaults to 1
    softmax     Softmax applied to an expression
    attn        Unmasked scaled dot-product attention: softmax(QK^T/sqrt(d_k)) V

For streaming, heavy hitters, and MPC resource bounds, combine fmom, supp, nrm,
prb/prx, exv, and the complexity templates. For coresets use relerr with the two
cost expressions; for adversarial perturbations use nrm, sbt, argmax, and grad.

Formula assumptions ~
These templates type notation; they do not establish a theorem's hypotheses.
    markov      Pr[X >= a] <= E[X]/a. Requires X >= 0 and a > 0.
    cheby       Pr[|X-E[X]| >= a] <= Var[X]/a^2. Requires finite variance,
                a > 0.
    chernoff    Pr[X >= (1+delta)mu] <= exp(-delta^2 mu/3). Requires X to be
                a sum of independent Bernoulli variables, mu = E[X], and
                0 < delta <= 1. This is the upper-tail form only.
    jl          Requires an embedding satisfying the displayed guarantee for
                the point pairs in question (and 0 < epsilon < 1).
    relerr      A template for a proved/required relative-error guarantee;
                use a nonnegative cost and 0 <= epsilon < 1. For a coreset,
                specify the quantification over all relevant queries/centers.
    dpineq      The DP condition must hold for every adjacent dataset pair and
                output event S; define adjacency in your notes.
    sens        D ~ D' denotes that chosen dataset-adjacency relation.
    fmom        Uses nonzero coordinates so p=0 counts distinct elements
                without evaluating 0^0; the usual moments have p >= 0.
    sgdstep     g_t denotes the chosen stochastic gradient estimator.
    attn        Softmax is row-wise; add a mask separately when required.

Notation references ~
    Differential privacy: Dwork and Roth, Definition 2.4
    https://www.cis.upenn.edu/~aaroth/Papers/privacybook.pdf
    Attention: Vaswani et al., equation (1)
    https://arxiv.org/html/1706.03762v7#S3.SS2.SSS1
    Streaming: MIT 6.854, lecture 5
    https://courses.csail.mit.edu/6.854/16/Notes/n5-streaming.html

All constructs use standard LaTeX or amsmath/amssymb. Add this to a document's
preamble when testing the full set: >tex
    \usepackage{amsmath,amssymb}
<
Example ~
In insert mode type mk, then ff, then x. Press CTRL-K, type y, then press CTRL-K
twice to leave both the fraction and inline math. The result is: >tex
    $\frac{x}{y}$
<
Snippet definitions live in LuaSnip/tex/. Context checks live in
lua/tex_context.lua. Tests use the installed plugins and type actual keys: >sh
    nvim --headless -u NONE -i NONE -l tests/test_tex_snippets.lua
<
Tests keep their output under /tmp/nvim-tex-snippets-* and never start a viewer.
